## What you did

- You traced Orbitly's iOS funnel drop (~8%) to a real bug: kestrel-ios 3.2.0 sends `event_id` as a per-session counter, so #240's dedupe treated distinct events as duplicates. ~1.18M legitimate Orbitly events were dropped since 13/11 (plus ~3.8k on Zest's pilot app) [1].
- You fixed the dedupe to key on `(project_id, device_id, event_id)` with tests, opened PR #247 with Maya as reviewer, and drafted a note asking the iOS team to restore UUID event_ids in 3.2.1 [1].
- You confirmed a post-deploy replay from landing can restore the ~1.18M Orbitly events (~40 min; a few seconds for Zest), skipping genuine replays [1].

## What changed

- Maya is ready to approve #247 once CI is green, but asks for the Orbitly drop count for Thursday's call with Orbitly — you already have it (~1.18M, ≈8.1% of their iOS volume) [2].
- Noa will present the finalized 12/11 postmortem at Friday's incident review (20/11); your root-cause section is in the final version [3].
- CI/Dockerfile moved to Go 1.23.4 in #245, merged [4].
- Zest confirmed their dashboards are complete after the backfill; Rachel closed their Zendesk ticket [6].

## What is still open

- PR #247 awaits CI and Maya's approval; once merged and deployed, run the Orbitly (and Zest) replay from 13/11 and watch `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total` for prj_0rb1 — you asked for a reminder [1].
- Action item from the review prep: add an alert when the ingest dead-letter queue exceeds 1,000 messages, before Friday's review [7].
- The iOS team note on restoring UUID event_ids still needs to be sent; the bug will recur otherwise [1].
